entries.subject: repo/c785042
entries.headline: don't crash when no browser opener binary exists (#12782)
entries.detail:
* fix(cli): don't crash on browser-open failure when no opener binary exists

open() with { wait: false } resolves to the detached child process before
the opener binary is known to exist. On hosts without one (e.g. xdg-open
on headless Linux), the failure arrives as an async 'error' event on the
listenerless child, escalating to an uncaughtException that kills the CLI
— bypassing every try/catch and .catch() at the call sites. Hitting
"Sign in with Cline" from the welcome screen reliably crashed the TUI in
containers.

Route all browser opens through a shared openUrlInBrowser() helper that
attaches the error listener and reports failure via its returned promise,
so flows fall back to their existing "visit the URL below" messaging.

* fix(cli): attach opener error listeners in the same tick as spawn

Greptile's review caught that the helper attached its listeners only after
awaiting open()'s promise. Empirically that window is safe under Node 22
(the listener wins) but real under Bun — the runtime the compiled CLI
ships on — where the missing-binary ENOENT 'error' event fires before the
microtask queue drains, reproducing the exact crash this helper exists to
prevent.

* fix(cli): don't let the ClinePass promo dialog trap users whose terminal drops Esc

The promo dialog could only be dismissed with Escape, and Esc is the
least reliable key across terminals: it arrives as a bare \x1b that

* fix(core): create checkpoints reliably across hosts, restarts, and compaction

#12691 moved checkpoint run-boundary detection into a beforeRun hook that
recorded snapshot.messages.length, assuming the run's user prompt is
appended afterwards. SessionRuntime (VS Code + CLI) instead seeds the
prompt into initialMessages and calls run(""), so the beforeRun delta is
always empty and no checkpoints were ever created in either surface.

already-checkpointed run), so a reopened session can't overwrite a good
pre-run snapshot with the mutated workspace. Run numbering uses the

entries.subject: repo/cf710d7
entries.headline: retry empty Ollama responses at the model boundary (#12845)
entries.detail:
Local backends (Ollama especially) intermittently return a turn that
finishes normally but carries no text, reasoning, or tool call. In the
SDK runtime an empty assistant turn is a hard failure ("Model returned
empty response"), so one flaky generation kills the whole task.

Adds a LanguageModelV3 middleware that retries the stream only when a
turn produced genuinely nothing, wired as the outermost middleware on
the Ollama vendor. A tool-call-only turn counts as content and is never
retried; non-empty turns stream through live with no added latency; and
turns that error or hit the token limit are passed through unchanged.

This is the streaming-safe slice of ai-sdk-ollama's reliability story:
its own reliability layer lives in doGenerate and owns the tool loop
(executes tools and force-synthesizes text), which is incompatible with
Cline running its own loop over doStream.

entries.headline: route webview persistence through a guarded storage boundary (#111)
entries.detail:
A blocked `localStorage` throws rather than returning null — Chrome under a
block-third-party-cookies policy, Safari private mode, and locked-down
enterprise profiles all raise SecurityError on plain property access.
`theme.ts` read it with no guard at all, and `syncHubTheme()` runs at boot, so
one of those testers got a blank page with no error at all. `nav-rail.ts` and
`model-selection.ts` had the `typeof window` guard but not the try/catch, so
they threw too.

`drive-feed-collapsed.ts` and `vscode.ts` already got this right, each with
their own copy of the guard. Rather than paste that a third and fourth time,
this adds `lib/safe-storage.ts` as the single boundary and routes every
preference module through it. Persisted webview state is preference data, not
correctness data, so a blocked store degrades to session-only: reads report
nothing stored, writes are dropped.

`vscode.ts` keeps its own guard — its getState/setState pair is the VS Code
API shim rather than a preference key, and it was already correct.

* feat(cli): add a self-hosted beta preflight to doctor

`doctor` answers "what is running and how do I kill it". A tester who has
just cloned the fork needs the question before that one: why will this not
work at all. Preflight checks Bun/Node against the pinned toolchain, whether
`bun install` and `bun run build:sdk` have been run, whether the hub daemon
(25463 / 25466) or dashboard (8787) ports are already held, and whether any
LLM provider is configured.

Two entry points, one implementation. The module imports node builtins only,
so `bun run preflight` works on a fresh clone before `bun install` — which is
exactly when "wrong Bun" and "nothing installed yet" are worth hearing.
`cline doctor preflight` runs the same checks after install and walks up to
the checkout root, because `bun run cli` sets cwd to `apps/cli`.

Port probing binds rather than shelling out to `lsof`, so unlike doctor's
existing PID listing it reports something on Windows. A busy port only fails
when CLINE_HUB_PORT / CLINE_HUB_DASHBOARD_PORT pins it; otherwise the server
relocates and a warning is the honest severity.

entries.subject: repo/a35d1ad
entries.headline: default posture across the four open ADRs (#136)
entries.detail:
Four ADRs each ended with open questions, and answering them one at a time
produces an incoherent product. This proposes one principle and derives all of
them from it.

The principle: sit on the safe side of every asymmetric axis, and the useful
side of every symmetric one. Money, audio, unattended writes and spawning are
asymmetric — too much is far worse than too little, so default conservative.
Showing a number, announcing an action, labelling a state are symmetric —
nothing bad happens from more, so default to showing.

Two corollaries worth more than they look. "Off by default" for everything is
not safety, it is cowardice — tts.enabled ships off with no in-product way to
turn it on, which is not a conservative default but an unfinished one. And
defaults teach: a muted mic tells a user "you control when you are heard" in
one interaction, which beats a tooltip.

The rule this codebase already earned the hard way: a default that fails
silently is the worst kind. The 9px stage, the fabricated Rooms list, the 3s
fallbacks producing a UI that looks fine and is lying — each was a quiet
default doing something plausible and wrong.

The Drive home view only listened for `call_error`, `room_snapshot`,

plus a listener for the transport's connectivity-failure text, so the
card always reaches a terminal state: "Hub is down. Could not check
the Pairing room." — matching the "Hub is down." copy PR #138 already

active call. The listener matches on the transport's "Cline Hub
server" wording rather than the bare `error` type, since that type is
also reused by unrelated server features (mic-mute gate, session
restore, drive commands) and would otherwise false-positive during the

resolveDriveVoiceTopology returned ok and Drive believed it had an LLM when no
credential was configured anywhere. assertTopologyLegal only compares egress
classes, so ADR-0010's fail-closed posture never fired for *unconfigured*,
only for *illegal*. Drive would open a call it could not complete.

The result type distinguishes the two cases rather than collapsing them.
`unconfigured` means no credential exists and the fix is to add one;

their topology is invalid, which is a worse bug than the one being fixed

entries.headline: bound chat-fork recursion generations (#146)
entries.detail:
* fix(drive): bound chat-fork recursion generations

Every completed/failed tool event fires runChatForkDirectorTick
best-effort, which claims forks with no depth counter, ancestry check,
or cycle guard. Worker sessions are room-linked, so their own tool
events re-enter the same path with parentSessionId set to the worker
itself -- recursion is capped in width (DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_CHAT_FORKS)
but unbounded in generations. See ADR-0023 decision 1.

- SeedPacketSchema/ChatForkRecordSchema (shared): add optional `depth`
  and a `refused` lifecycle + `refusal` reason, so ancestry and
  suppression are part of the persisted record, not just checked
  in-flight.

entries.subject: repo/20b28bb
entries.headline: scope secret dirty tracking per provider (#156)
entries.detail:
The provider detail panel stays mounted across provider switches, so #147
wiped the shared dirty-field set whenever provider.id changed. That kept an
untouched field on the next provider from committing blank and destroying its
stored credential, but it also discarded the record that the user had cleared
the previous provider's key. Switching away and back fell through to the stale
server-side provider.apiKeyPresent, so a deleted key rendered as "saved" and
the OAuth login button stayed hidden until a catalog reload.

Replace the single Set plus wipe-on-switch with a Map keyed by provider id.
Nothing is cleared on a switch, so a cleared key stays cleared, and a lookup
can only ever see the paths dirtied for that one provider, so dirtiness still
cannot leak across providers.

The presence and commit-eligibility decisions move into a pure
secret-field-state module that both copies of the component import, since the
hub's vitest config is node-only and excludes .tsx.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
